messages.subject: Re: Rotation of orthophoto
parts:
Hi Pedja,

I guess it is only a visualization artifect. 
The image is similar to the first one, however with the plot orientation straight.
The average result per plot should be the same. 

To make a test, you can use the function fieldPolygon to draw a shapefile in the same region (same plots) in both images. Then, you can use the function fiendInfo to extract the data and compare it.

Here is the link showing how to do it: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P15

Let me know if the results changed.
Best
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: Rotation of orthophoto
parts:
Hi Pedja,

Maybe the images have different geographical references or they were taken in different days. Are you using GCPs for overlay images?

This error is because your shapefile=EX1 is selecting region outside of mosaic=DEM0 dimentions (shapefile must be smaller and inside the mosaic). Are you sure that you are using the same  rotation theta in both images (EX1 and DEM)? Also, EX1 and DEM are from the same processes of orthomosaicing (because this two images must have the same geographic reference)? 

And yes, you can use jpg images as field shape for DEM.

All the best,
Filipe
